newsitem.title: UK: BA moves Paris flights in Air Algeria security row.
newsitem.headline: BA moves Paris flights in Air Algeria security row.

text.p: British Airways said on Saturday it had diverted some flights away from Charles de Gaulle airport at Paris after French authorities allowed the state airline of strife-torn Algeria to resume operations.

BA said it would take legal action to overturn the airport's decision to allow Air Algerie to operate from one of the main terminals at Charles de Gaulle, a move it alleges threatened the security of other carriers.
A BA spokesman said two of its flights destined for Charles de Gaulle on Saturday morning had landed at Orly airport to the south of the French capital and more might follow.

When Air Algerie restarted flights to Charles de Gaulle on Friday it was operating from one of the main terminals along with other major carrier. It stopped flying to Paris two years ago in protest at being forced to use a remote terminal.
BA alleges the security arrangements for Air Algerie at Charles de Gaulle fell short of those at Marseille and other French airports where the airline operated.
About 60,000 people have died in Algeria in widespread violence sparked by the cancellation of January 1992 election which Moslem fundamentalists were set to win.
